doc.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Coltrane at Birdland and an Albert Ayler concert
summary: He found Coltrane's long solos intense and endured three hours of Albert Ayler.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Did Coltrane’s music appeal to you at that time?

Something very interesting about it, yeah. They take these long solos. I think I heard a half hour or forty-five minute solo at Birdland, you know it just goes on and on and on and on. I says I couldn’t figure out exactly, it was pretty intense stuff. I remember another intense thing when I was in New York. I went down to hear an Albert Ayler concert.
And I stayed there for three hours and I almost threw up because it seemed like they were just [scats] doing all these out things. I says what the heck are they talking about? What does this mean?
But I had to go down and hear it for myself, you know I was interested in some of the records of Albert Ayler and this type of stuff.
And you stayed for three hours, huh?

I stayed for three hours because they had several people do whole — it sounded like they would do — I mean all sorts of odd-like, just like, well it sounded angry. But some of it was very interesting, then some of it perhaps not.
That’s very diplomatic of you. Perhaps not. You even did, to backtrack just a touch, you did some gigs with Tommy Dorsey and a few of the big bands?
